author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Thick haze from fires disrupted flights for several days on Indonesia’s portion of Borneo, the Associated Press reported Monday. Visibility in parts of West Kalimantan fell below one kilometer, creating problems for aircraft operations and worsening conditions for residents.

The fires have burned for about a month during a prolonged dry period. More than 202,000 hectares were reported burned across Indonesia from January through July, according to the AP report. Smoke has also prompted school suspensions in other areas as officials monitor pollution levels.

Firefighters have been working to contain the outbreaks, with international support involved in the response. The flight disruptions and reduced visibility remained developing conditions, and authorities continued to assess where the smoke was thickest and how the fires were spreading.
Air travelers were advised to check with carriers because conditions can change quickly when smoke and visibility shift. Officials continued to monitor the affected airports as the haze moved.
dek: Smoke from fires in West Kalimantan disrupted flights for several days as thick haze reduced visibility and raised air-quality concerns.
headline: Thick haze disrupts flights on Indonesia’s Borneo island
